correctness.rationale: PASS: Orthogonal energy decomposition f_i=m+d(s/L_i-1/2)+g_i with Dirichlet g_i shows the parallel-edge Green diagonal Q_B=C+(1/L_i-1/T)s(L_i-s)+(s/L_i-1/2)^2/c; pinching d to zero gives rose Q_R without final term. The coefficient of s(L_i-s) in Q_B is ((T-L_i)(c-1/L_i)-1)/(T(1+L_i(c-1/L_i))), strictly positive for r≥3 via Cauchy–Schwarz, while for r=2 it vanishes. Hence maxima for r≥3 are longest-edge midpoints on both graphs, K=C+M(T-M)/(4T), and r=2 banana is everywhere norming while rose only loop midpoints, both K=T/12. Midpoint Green representers coincide because the extra d-mode vanishes. Independent exact rational substitution L=(1,2,3) gives K=11/24; source independent nodal Poisson checker uses exact SymPy solves for seven families (finite corroboration).

originality.rationale: FAIL: Two earlier full published theorems already determine both sharp constants and all maximizers for these exact metric graphs. The November 8 longest-parallel-path theorem gives exactly K_B=C+M(T-M)/(4T) and midpoint localization; the November 8 flower/rose theorem provides Q_R=C+(1/L_i-1/T)s(L_i-s) on a single hub (its proof without pendants) and K_R with the same formula. The general cactus Green formula is an additional encompassing reference for bouquet loops. Equating the already explicit constants gives pinching invariance immediately; the Green representers at midpoints coincide by deleting the prior parallel-potential d term. These straightforward implications cover the new central assertion despite different wording.
